description: A single-panel figure rendered as a data table (no axes, no graph; one image block). The table has seven rows and six data columns. The header column lists, in order: "Engineering strain (%)", "True strain (%)", "σ_dis(γ) , (RT), MPa", "σ_dis(α) , (RT-GND), MPa", "σ_dis(γ) , (LNT), MPa", "σ_dis(α) , (LNT-GND), MPa", "σ_twin(γ) , (LNT), MPa". The six column headers are the deformation levels Engineering strain (%) = 3.0, 10.0, 20.0, 28.0, 38.0 and 55.0, with the corresponding True strain (%) = 3.0, 9.5, 18.2, 24.7, 32.2 and 43.8. Dislocation strengthening of the γ phase is tabulated at RT as 48, 207, 347, 434, 474, and "–" MPa, and at LNT as 58, 240, 379, 469, 504 and 646 MPa. The α-phase GND contributions are small: 1, 4, 6, 8, 8 and "–" MPa at RT-GND, and 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9 MPa at LNT-GND. The σ_twin(γ) (LNT) row contains "–" for all strains up to 38.0 % and a single value of 290 MPa at 55.0 % engineering strain. The figure quantifies how the individual strengthening terms (dislocation, GND and twinning) build up the flow stress of a Fe35Mn6Al0.1C low-carbon low-density cryogenic steel as deformation proceeds, showing LNT terms exceed RT ones and twinning contributes only at the largest strain.

subfigures.description: A single unlabelled data table (no sub-panels): 7 rows × 6 data columns listing engineering strain, true strain and the strengthening contributions σ_dis(γ) (RT and LNT), σ_dis(α) (RT-GND and LNT-GND) and σ_twin(γ) (LNT) in MPa; the only σ_twin entry is 290 MPa at 55.0 % engineering strain.

observations.observation: The table has six deformation columns headed by Engineering strain (%) = 3.0, 10.0, 20.0, 28.0, 38.0, 55.0, and corresponding True strain (%) = 3.0, 9.5, 18.2, 24.7, 32.2, 43.8.
σ_dis(γ) at RT increases monotonically from 48 MPa at 3.0 % to 207, 347, 434 and 474 MPa at 10.0, 20.0, 28.0 and 38.0 % engineering strain, with no value entered (dash) at 55.0 %.
σ_dis(γ) at LNT is 58, 240, 379, 469, 504 and 646 MPa across the same six strain levels, i.e. higher than the RT value at every strain where both are given.
σ_dis(α) (RT-GND) is very small, listed as 1, 4, 6, 8 and 8 MPa for 3.0-38.0 % engineering strain and dashed at 55.0 %.
σ_dis(α) (LNT-GND) is listed as 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9 MPa for the six strain levels.
The σ_twin(γ) (LNT) row is dashed at 3.0, 10.0, 20.0, 28.0 and 38.0 % engineering strain and has a single value of 290 MPa at 55.0 %.
The figure is a table only; it contains no plotted curves, error bars or graphical axes.
The caption states that the table presents the strengthening contribution of σ_dis and σ_twin strengthening to the flow stress.
The caption's row labels distinguish room-temperature (RT) terms from liquid-nitrogen-temperature (LNT) terms and label the α-phase terms as GND (geometrically necessary dislocation) contributions.

The paper studies a low-carbon low-density Fe35Mn6Al0.1C steel at room temperature (RT) and liquid nitrogen temperature (LNT), so the RT/LNT columns refer to these two test temperatures of the same alloy.

By subtraction of the tabulated terms, the largest strain of 55.0 % engineering strain (43.8 % true strain) at LNT carries 646 MPa of γ dislocation strengthening plus 290 MPa of γ twinning strengthening, whereas the corresponding RT dislocation term is not tabulated.
